newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hesse warns DM could weaken ahead of EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Hesse warns DM could weaken ahead of EMU start.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse warned on Tuesday that the German mark could see some weakness in the run-up to European monetary union, as some investors may switch holdings into other currencies.

In a speech to a reception at the Hamburg-based regional central bank of which he is president, Hesse said that this possibility arose because around 30 to 40 percent of marks in circulation were held abroad.

"No one can predict whether these mark holdings will be held until the start of monetary union and then exchanged into euros or will be exchanged earlier into other currencies," Hesse said according to the text of a speech.
"Mark weakness for this reason cannot be ruled out with absolute certainty," he added.
Europe plans to launch a single currency from January 1, 1999, melding together the currencies of those countries which meet certain economic requirements.
In his speech, Hesse said that certain action ought to be taken as soon as possible to convince markets and the general public that there was no cause for concern about Europe's currency plans.
One such step which should be taken was an early agreement on the procedure by which the conversion rates for national currencies into the euro will be set.
He warned that delay in deciding this could lead to markets implementing a "final depreciation" in some currencies.
A text of the speech was released in advance.

A further important issue would be for the Bundesbank to make clear that it remained fully committed to a stabiility policy right up until it hands over responsibility for monetary policy to the new European Central Bank at the start of 1999.
